mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship is observed in historical data where periods of low interest rates consistently precede positive equity returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day S&P 500 return when UNRATE increases > 0.3pp over 3 months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return when both HOUST and RSAFS decline (relative to their 3-month moving averages) is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-recession recovery phase (defined by sustained GDP growth above 1.0% and declining unemployment), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a potential slowdown in manufacturing activity, which is typically followed by positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates policy support.
failure_condition: The average 60-day S&P 500 return when INDPRO declines (relative to the previous month) and GDPC1 growth rate (year-over-year) > 1.0% and UNRATE < 5.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten policy.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a severe labor market deterioration, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day S&P 500 return when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS declines > 0.5% (relative to the previous month) is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by GDP growth above 2.0% and low unemployment), a decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an imminent slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day S&P 500 return when GDPC1 growth (quarter-over-quarter) declines (relative to the previous quarter) in a late-cycle expansion (defined by UNRATE < 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 (relative to the 2017 base) signals a manufacturing slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return when INDPRO < 105.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) over the last 5 years.
